notes: wowsims-forever models one Hunter spell package for all three specs (engine spec mapping, design section on the APL rotation lane); Beast Mastery, Marksmanship and Survival share this same Aimed Shot / Multi-Shot weave and differ mainly in which cooldowns and secondary shots they lean on. The cited Warcraft Tavern BM guide's own numbered rotation (step 7) says to cast and refresh Serpent Sting -- it only calls Arcane Shot a leveling-only filler, not Serpent Sting -- so Serpent Sting upkeep is kept here, in the same shape as hunter-marksmanship's. Bestial Wrath is added as the spec's own cooldown, timed with Rapid Fire so both land in the one burst window a Classic-length fight allows. Every rank named here is checked against this build's own spellconst: the fork's p1.apl.json preset names Multi-Shot as spell 25294, which does not exist in this build at all (Multi-Shot only has one rank here, 2643), and calls Serpent Sting rank 8 when 25295 is actually rank 9 in this build's spellconst -- both fixed here rather than copied stale. Aimed Shot (20904) is registered by the engine again since 2026-09-28 (its registration had been commented out, and the cast line was declared inert until then). What did need fixing: nothing in this site's request pipeline (sim/request) ever sets a character's DistanceFromTarget, so every hunter starts at 0 -- under Multi-Shot, Serpent Sting and Aimed Shot's own ExtraCastCondition floor of 12 (core.MinRangedAttackDistance), which also gates the ranged auto-attack itself (sim/core/attack.go's startPull). A `move` prepull action to 30 yards is added so this and every future simulation of this spec actually has a ranged auto-attack and can cast its ranged abilities. Under this smoke build specifically (no gear equipped anywhere) the ranged weapon's SwingSpeed is the Weapon{} zero value, which collapses the ranged swing timer to its 500ms cast-time floor (sim/core/attack.go's WeaponAttack.updateSwingDuration: curSwingDuration = weapon.SwingSpeed / hasteMultiplier = 0) -- a real ranged weapon's positive SwingSpeed does not have this problem. The resulting sub-GCD auto-shot loop saturates the character's action economy so completely that the priority list, including Multi-Shot and Serpent Sting, never gets a decision window in this one bare-weapon run; this is a new engine-side artifact of the no-gear smoke build (recorded for the engine ledger), not a defect in this rotation's gates. Rotation-accuracy program diagnosis (2026-09-28), inert 2643 and 3045: both are unranked single-id abilities in spellranks.json (Multi-Shot's rank-1 id 2643 is the ONLY row spellranks.json carries for this ability in this build -- its higher client ranks 14288/14289/14290/25294 are simply absent from the data entirely -- and Rapid Fire 3045 is genuinely a single, unranked ability), each with rank:0 and a real nonzero level column (2643 at 18, 3045 at 26) that the ladder's own idLearnLevel deliberately skips for EVERY rank<=0 row (the same skip that correctly keeps Bloodrage/Judgement -- true always-known, no engine level gate at all -- from being wrongly treated as gated). Multi-Shot and Rapid Fire are the opposite case: sim/hunter/multi_shot.go's rank 1 carries RequiredLevel 18, and sim/hunter/rapid_fire.go's registerRapidFire returns immediately `if hunter.Level < 26`, so the engine really does gate both on a level spellranks.json's rank<=0 shape cannot express to this harness. Fix round: not declared inert here (that would wrongly tell the level-60 smoke test to expect them permanently unresolved, when the pinned engine resolves both fine above their real gate). Fixed instead with a small, explicit, engine-verified allowlist in sim/internal/spellranks (singleTierLevelOverrides) and its read-only ladder-side mirror (sim/request/ladder.go's idLearnLevel): only these two ids (plus druid-feral's Tiger's Fury, the same shape) are promoted from 'untracked, always learned' to a real single-tier gate, so Bloodrage (spellranks.json row: level 10, rank 0) and Judgement (level 4, rank 0) are untouched -- neither is actually level-gated by the engine at all (checked directly: sim/warrior/bloodrage.go and sim/paladin/judgement.go register unconditionally), so a blanket 'rank 0 with Level>0 means level-gated' rule would have wrongly broken them. See this lane's report for the fuller diagnosis and the data-pipeline follow-up (Multi-Shot's own higher client ranks 14288/14289/14290/25294 are simply missing from spellranks.json entirely, a separate gap from this level-10 false unresolved). 2026-10-21 (ladder rotations lane): Arcane Shot also fires while Aimed Shot cannot start (the next auto shot is within a second, which is Aimed Shot's own gate). At level 50 the ladder's 1.6 second ranged weapon never leaves a window for Aimed Shot, which then sat ready forever and held Arcane Shot behind it, so the shot never fired. 2026-10-31 (theorycraft audit fixes): Multi-Shot and Aimed Shot share one 6 second cooldown in Forever (client spell category 2; both tooltips say so), and the engine now runs them on one timer. On that shared timer the instant Multi-Shot outdamages Aimed Shot, whose 2 second cast pauses the auto shot, so Multi-Shot fires on every cooldown and Aimed Shot is only the pre-pull opener. The lines that used to read Aimed Shot's cooldown now read Multi-Shot's, the same clock. Client 1.60.1.70707 (2026-10-31): Aspect of the Hawk's ranks 1-5 fell to 15/22/30/38/47 ranged attack power, so rank 6 (14322, 55) is the strongest from level 58 and the prepull casts it; through 70685 rank 5 (90) was, and rank 6 was skipped as inferior. 2026-11-03 (sim-accuracy round 13, server hotfix push for 1.60.1.70753): Aimed Shot about doubled at every rank, Arcane Shot, Serpent Sting, Aspect of the Hawk and Trueshot Aura went up. Aimed Shot now takes the shared cooldown whenever the next auto shot is more than 1.2 seconds away, and Multi-Shot only when the cast would hold an auto shot; measured beyond error at seeds 1 and 50001. 2026-11-04 (sim-accuracy round 20): Blizzard's 3 November notes put 15% of ranged attack power on Arcane Shot and 5% a tick on Serpent Sting, so Multi-Shot is now the worst shot for its mana. Multi-Shot waits while mana is under a quarter and Arcane Shot's own mana gate is gone; measured beyond error at seeds 1 and 50001 on 180 s and on 420 s fights.

sources.label: wowsims-forever default hunter priority list (shared across all three hunter specs; Multi-Shot and Serpent Sting ranks corrected against this build)
Warcraft Tavern: Classic Beast Mastery Hunter rotation (Aimed Shot on cooldown, Serpent Sting refreshed, Multi-Shot filler, Bestial Wrath and Rapid Fire together as the one burst window)
Forever Sixty default rotation, unvalidated until the nightly job runs

priorityList.notes: Hunter's Mark whenever the target is not marked. One mark per target is enough: if another hunter's mark is already up, leave it.

Bestial Wrath on the pull with Rapid Fire and your trinkets, then again every two minutes. The pet hits 50% harder for 18 seconds and shrugs off fear, so send it in first and press it once the pet is on the boss.

Rapid Fire on the pull with Bestial Wrath, as an auto shot leaves and Multi-Shot is about to come back. The haste starts on a fresh shot and the first Multi-Shot lands inside it. It is a five minute cooldown, so a boss fight gets one: put your trinkets and racial on the same press.

Aimed Shot when the shared cooldown comes up right after an auto shot fires. For Beast Mastery it is only a small extra over Multi-Shot, and Multi-Shot on every cooldown is fine. If you are partway to your next auto shot, take Multi-Shot and keep the auto rolling.

Multi-Shot on the shared cooldown when Aimed Shot's cast would hold an auto shot, while you are above a quarter of your mana. It is instant, so it never delays your next shot, but it is the worst damage for its mana you fire, so it is the first shot to go when the mana runs low.

Serpent Sting when it has under 1.5 seconds left and Multi-Shot is not about to come back. Refreshing any earlier throws away a tick. Every tick carries 5% of your ranged attack power on top of its own damage, so it is the best damage for its mana you fire: keep it rolling for the whole fight. When both are ready, Multi-Shot goes first: a late Multi-Shot pushes back the shared cooldown, while a late sting costs only a moment of its damage.

Arcane Shot to fill a gap when Multi-Shot is more than a global away. It is instant and never holds an auto shot, and every hit carries 15% of your ranged attack power, so it is second only to Serpent Sting for damage per mana: keep it going even when the mana runs low.
